            <h2>US amount and point unit</h2>
            <p>At the Bronze base rate, eligible pre-tax spending earns 1 point per $1 in the US, so $50 is about 50 points before any eligible promotion. Google rounds points per item, so actual results can differ when purchases are split.</p>
        </section>
        <section class="section">
            <h2>Next step</h2>
            <p>Compare the result with the points still needed for your next level, then confirm the eligible amount and offer terms in Google Play before buying.</p>
        </section>
        <section class="section">
            <h2>How to read this estimate</h2>
            <p>Use the result to match planned purchases with the confirmed earning rate available to your account. Check eligible items and the offer period in Google Play, then recalculate the remaining progress after points are credited.</p>
        </section>

        <section class="section lp-faq">
            <h2>FAQ</h2>
            <details><summary>Is $50 before or after tax?</summary><p>Use the eligible item price before tax. Google excludes tax from Play Points calculations in the US.</p></details>
            <details><summary>Can I use this outside the US?</summary><p>Use your local-currency PlayPoint page and the earning rate shown for your country or account. This preset is for US dollars.</p></details>
            <details><summary>Do gift cards earn points?</summary><p>Buying or redeeming a gift card does not by itself mean the card amount earns Play Points. Check how the eligible Google Play purchase is treated in your account.</p></details>
        </section>
